title: Sign in to a remote MCP server that requires OAuth
contract: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE through the MCP SDK, owned by a single manager (`tools/mcp_oauth_manager.py`) that is the only place a provider is instantiated: per-server token files under `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/`, transparent refresh with re-auth only on refresh failure, an mtime disk watch so a token refreshed by another process is picked up without restart, and in-flight-future dedup so N concurrent 401s trigger one recovery. Client identity is a published Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) with recorded per-server rejection falling back to DCR; callback ports pinned to 27890–27894 and held as bound sockets so an exact-match redirect can work on a first login, reverting to a random port under nine documented conditions; a dashboard-mediated callback bridge relocates the two human/browser hops for headless installs without moving any crypto; and an `oauth:` sub-block overrides client_id/secret/name/auth-method/redirect and a token-endpoint-only user_agent (acp-mcp-dev.mcp-oauth, .mcp-oauth-cimd, .mcp-oauth-ports, .mcp-key-oauth-block, .mcp-dashboard-oauth, .mcp-oauth-manager).
governance: read-only in itself, but it mints and stores durable credentials — tokens belong in the existing secret scope (agents/core/routers/secrets.py, agents/core/vault.py), never in settings storage, and each acquisition should leave an audit row.

- CIMD (Client ID Metadata Document) client identity with DCR fallback
- pinned loopback callback ports held as bound sockets for a first-login exact-match redirect
- the remaining owner overrides: client name, token-endpoint auth method and token-endpoint user agent
- a public-suffix list for the issuer-domain check (today: last two labels, three under a ccTLD's generic second level)

title: Let an MCP server ask the agent for an LLM completion or for user input mid-call
contract: `sampling:` gives a server `sampling/createMessage` with a per-instance handler: enabled flag, model override and `allowed_models` list, `max_tokens_cap` (4096), timeout (30 s), `max_rpm` (10) on a 60-second sliding window, `max_tool_rounds` (5), log level, and tracked request/error/token/tool-use metrics. `elicitation:` lets a server ask the user for structured input mid-tool-call and routes it through `tools.approval.prompt_dangerous_approval` so it surfaces on whichever channel owns the session; URL-mode is cleanly declined; the schema field is read under both mcp-1.x and mcp-2.0 spellings; everything fails closed to decline/cancel (acp-mcp-dev.mcp-key-sampling, .mcp-key-elicitation).
governance: sampling spends the owner's model budget on a third party's behalf: it must cross the existing budget ledger (agents/core/kernel/budget.py) and be per-server rate-limited. Elicitation must land in the approval queue, fail closed on timeout, and never auto-accept.

title: Authorize an outbound MCP tool call before it runs

title: Refuse a malicious MCP server config or a poisoned tool description
contract: Three layers. `hermes_cli/mcp_security.py` validates every entry at save time *and* at spawn time against a hardcoded IOC list (the June-2026 hermes-0day SSH key prefix and source IPs), shell-interpreter-plus-network-egress shapes, and OS-persistence shapes (authorized_keys, /etc/cron, .bashrc, pam_*.so, systemd). `_scan_mcp_description` runs ten patterns over every tool description before it reaches the model's context ('ignore previous instructions', role-tag injection, concealment, network commands, base64 decode, exec/eval, dangerous imports). Plus an OSV malware preflight on stdio packages with two nested timeouts and fail-open, `strip_unicode_tags` on descriptions and schemas so invisible tag characters cannot smuggle instructions, and a two-tier result cap (2 M-char hard truncation above a 50 K spillover threshold, 50 MiB per resource) (acp-mcp-dev.mcp-security-validator, .mcp-injection-scan, .mcp-osv-preflight, .mcp-result-caps).
governance: read-only checks that gate a privileged effect: a validator finding must refuse the save and the spawn, not merely warn, and a description-scan hit should quarantine the server the way agents/core/security/quarantine.py handles skills.

title: Keep a flaky or slow MCP server from wedging or slowing the whole product
contract: Discovery starts in a daemon thread at process start with a cheap config probe so non-MCP users never import the stack, then a bounded join at the one place the tool snapshot is taken, with a retry-after-zero-connected allowance; a fingerprinted schema cache (`$HERMES_HOME/cache/mcp_schema_cache.json`, mode 0600, honouring the server's SEP-2549 ttlMs) plus lazy connect registers a server's tools with no subprocess until the first real call; reconnection is three layers — jittered exponential backoff (5 retries, 60 s ceiling, ±20 %), a per-server connect cooldown (30 s → 600 s) and a circuit breaker (3 failures, 60 s) — with a parked state that self-probes every 300 s; plus keepalive pings, stdio idle/lifetime recycling, a POSIX parent-death watchdog supervisor that kills the child's process group when Hermes dies hard, stderr redirected to a shared log so it cannot corrupt a TUI, an orphan reaper sweeping by parentage, a cross-process advisory discovery lock, and one `get_mcp_status()` feeding all four UIs (acp-mcp-dev.mcp-startup, .mcp-schema-cache, .mcp-lazy-connect, .mcp-reconnect, .mcp-shutdown, .mcp-discovery-lock, .mcp-status-api, .mcp-stderr-log, .mcp-stdio-watchdog, .mcp-key-keepalive, .mcp-key-lifecycle).
governance: read-only. One caveat: a lazily-registered tool from a schema cache is advertised before the server is verified, so the fingerprint must cover every connection-defining field and the outbound authorization gate must run on the live call, not on registration.
remaining_verbatim:
- fingerprinted schema cache (0600, honouring ttlMs) and lazy connect on first call; Hermes's tools/mcp_schema_cache.py was not adopted because its fingerprint omits cwd, env, headers and the trust tier and it needs two new compat shims
- stdio idle/lifetime recycling
- parent-death watchdog killing the child's process group, orphan reaper
- cross-process discovery lock
- a separate per-server connect cooldown (30 s → 600 s); the breaker and backoff cover most of it

title: Make a third-party tool schema safe and unambiguous for every model provider
contract: `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` repairs a server's JSON Schema once, provider-agnostically, at registration: draft-07 `definitions` promoted to `$defs` contextually (only as a meta-keyword, never when it is a property name, because `$` in a property name 400s Anthropic and OpenAI); missing/null `type` on an object-shaped node coerced; empty `properties` added so `required` cannot dangle; `required` pruned to names that exist (Gemini 400s otherwise); Pydantic nullable `anyOf` unions collapsed to the non-null branch. Names are sanitized and prefixed to `mcp__<server>__<tool>` with everything outside [A-Za-z0-9_] replaced, matching Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode, while filters still match the original names (acp-mcp-dev.mcp-schema-normalize, .mcp-tool-naming).
governance: read-only, but the prefix is a security property too: an unprefixed third-party tool can shadow a built-in tool name and intercept calls meant for a governed path.
